title: Ratio and proportion
ks3: Ratio, proportion and rates of change: ratio, sharing, direct and inverse proportion, scales
intro: Mixing drinks, sharing sweets, scaling recipes and reading maps. Practise ratios, sharing in a ratio, proportion and scale.
description: Free KS3 Maths ratio and proportion questions with answers: simplifying ratios, sharing in a ratio, recipes, best buys, inverse proportion and map scales. Marked instantly, for ages 9 to 14.

questions.q: A bag has 3 red sweets and 5 blue sweets. What is the ratio of red to blue?
questions.hint: Write red first, because the question says "red to blue".
questions.explain: There are 3 red and 5 blue, so red : blue = 3 : 5.

questions.q: Which ratio is the same as 1 : 4?
questions.hint: Multiply both parts by the same number.
questions.explain: 1 : 4 multiplied by 3 is 3 : 12. (2 : 6 is the same as 1 : 3.)

questions.hint: Divide both parts by the biggest number that goes into both.

questions.q: A drink is made with squash and water in the ratio 2 : 3. What fraction of the drink is squash?
questions.hint: How many parts are there altogether?
questions.explain: There are 2 + 3 = 5 parts and 2 of them are squash, so {2/5} of the drink is squash.

questions.q: Share £30 in the ratio 1 : 2. How much is the bigger share, in pounds?
questions.hint: How many parts altogether? How much is one part worth?
questions.explain: 1 + 2 = 3 parts. One part = £30 ÷ 3 = £10. The bigger share is 2 parts = £20.

questions.q: Squash and water are mixed in the ratio 2 : 3. How much water is needed for 100 ml of squash?
questions.hint: 2 parts are 100 ml. How much is 1 part?
questions.explain: 2 parts = 100 ml, so 1 part = 50 ml. Water is 3 parts = 150 ml.

questions.q: Ann and Bo share 48 sweets in the ratio 5 : 3. How many sweets does Ann get?
questions.explain: One part = 48 ÷ 8 = 6 sweets. Ann gets 5 × 6 = 30 and Bo gets 3 × 6 = 18.

questions.q: The ratio of boys to girls in a club is 4 : 5. There are 20 boys. How many children are in the club altogether?
questions.hint: 4 parts are 20 boys. How many is one part?
questions.explain: 4 parts = 20, so one part = 5. Girls = 5 × 5 = 25. Altogether 20 + 25 = 45 children.

questions.q: 3 pencils cost 60p. How much do 5 pencils cost, in pence?
questions.hint: Find the cost of 1 pencil first.

questions.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 200 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 6 people?
questions.hint: Work out the flour for 1 person, or for 2 people.
questions.explain: For 2 people you need 100 g, so for 6 people you need 3 × 100 = 300 g.

questions.hint: Work out the cost of 100 g for each.
questions.explain: 500 g for £2.00 is 40p per 100 g. 200 g for £1.00 is 50p per 100 g. So the 500 g pack is better value.

questions.q: 4 painters take 6 hours to paint a fence. How long would 3 painters take, working at the same speed?
questions.hint: Fewer painters take longer. How long would 1 painter take?
questions.explain: 1 painter would take 4 × 6 = 24 hours. 3 painters take 24 ÷ 3 = 8 hours. This is inverse proportion.

questions.q: A tap fills a 12-litre bucket in 3 minutes. How long does it take to fill a 20-litre bucket?
questions.hint: How many litres does the tap fill each minute?

questions.q: A map has a scale of 1 : 50,000. Two places are 2 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they in real life, in kilometres?
questions.hint: 1 cm on the map is 50,000 cm in real life. 100,000 cm = 1 km.

questions.q: A model car is made to a scale of 1 : 20. The model is 21 cm long. How long is the real car, in metres?
questions.hint: The real car is 20 times as long.
